body:
Rachel Kim: Heads up from Support — beta customer (AcmeAI) is confused about variant naming + “control” semantics in Route A/B. They expected “control” = “existing production behavior” (i.e., no experiment override), but in Console they saw “Control” and assumed that means “not participating in experiment / always their pinned model”.

Rachel Kim: Quote from call notes: “If Control is using our current pinned model, why is it labeled as a variant? We thought Control meant the baseline route config and Variant B is the only one changing.”

Rachel Kim: They also got tripped up by default labels “Variant A / Variant B”. They renamed them to “control” and “treatment” but then weren’t sure which one gets the larger traffic % when they set 90/10.

Rachel Kim: Repro on our side: create experiment -> variants show A/B; user edits names; results page shows “control” but no explanation that “control” is just a user-provided label and not special logic.

Rachel Kim: Link they were reading (draft docs): https://github.com/redwood-docs/pull/2217 (Route-level A/B testing docs PR)

Simran Kaur: +1, I heard similar from another design partner last week. They want “baseline” to clearly mean: the one you compare against, not “no experiment”.

Marissa Cole: Thanks. In our PRD we used “control” loosely, but Console currently treats both as equal “variants” (no special logic besides your allocations). We probably need to be explicit in UI + docs.

Wei Chen: Looking at PR 2217, we currently say “Control (Variant A)” in a few places but we never define what “control” means, and we don’t say it’s not automatic.

Elliot Price: Agree. Doc tweak proposal:
- Replace “control” language with “baseline” by default.
- Add callout: “Variants are labels only; Redwood does not infer baseline from the name ‘control’.”
- Add an example section: “Keeping current behavior as baseline” (pin current model/config as Variant A) and “Testing new model as Variant B”.

Kenji Nakamura: On UI: we can add helper text next to variant names:
“Variant names are for display only. ‘Control’ has no special behavior; choose your baseline by setting allocations and selecting the configuration.”

Dylan Brooks: From eng perspective, +1. We should also consider changing default labels from “Variant A/B” to “Baseline / Candidate” in Console (copy-only change). That’s safer than adding semantics.

Rachel Kim: That would help Support a lot. The customer also asked: “Is Variant A always the thing Redwood recommends?” They assumed “A” implies “primary”.

Marissa Cole: Let’s do two changes:
1) Docs: update terminology + add the explicit callout.
2) Console copy: replace A/B defaults with Baseline/Candidate + add small tooltip.

Wei Chen: I can patch the docs today. Can someone confirm final copy for the callout?

Elliot Price: Suggested callout text (feel free to edit):
“Baseline vs candidate: Redwood treats all variants the same. The label ‘control’ does not enable special behavior. Choose your baseline by explicitly configuring it as a variant (e.g., your currently pinned model) and assigning traffic.”

Kenji Nakamura: :thumbsup: Works. For UI tooltip we can shorten: “Names are display-only; ‘control’ has no special meaning.”

Dylan Brooks: I’ll file a small UI copy task against DES-142 / ENG-2843 follow-up. This is low risk and can go in the beta patch.

Simran Kaur: Also worth adding to troubleshooting: if they want “existing prod” as baseline, they should copy the current route config into Variant Baseline. People assume it’s implicit.

Wei Chen: Cool, I’ll add a “Common setup” section with that exact workflow + screenshot placeholders.

Rachel Kim: Thanks all. I’ll reply to AcmeAI with: “Control is just a label today; set your pinned model as the baseline variant.” and point them at the updated docs once merged.

Marissa Cole: Please do, and flag if they still feel blocked. We can also rename “control” in results tables in the near term.

Elliot Price: Ping me when you’ve replied — I want to make sure Support messaging matches the docs.

Rachel Kim: Will do. (Also adding note to SUP queue so other agents don’t tell customers “control is special”.)

Dylan Brooks: :eyes: please link the SUP ticket when you have it.

Rachel Kim: It’s currently in HubSpot notes, but I’ll open a Jira Support ticket and drop it here.
